verdict: Palantir's revenue grew 93% to $1.9B as U.S. commercial sales jumped 149% — and more than half of every revenue dollar ended as net profit.

segments.name: Government
segments.note: Software for the U.S. military, intelligence agencies and allied governments — still the biggest customer group; U.S. government revenue alone grew 90% to $809M.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.note: Software for companies — U.S. commercial revenue jumped 149% to $764M as businesses raced to put AI to work, and Palantir closed a record $2.13B of U.S. commercial contract value.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and the 'bootcamp' try-before-you-buy push that has been winning commercial customers.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platforms — Gotham, Foundry and the AIP AI layer.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company: legal, finance and offices.

takeaways.title: U.S. businesses are the growth engine
takeaways.text: U.S. commercial revenue hit $764M and Palantir closed a record $2.13B of U.S. commercial contract value in a single quarter — the deal pipeline behind future revenue.

takeaways.title: Half of revenue became profit
takeaways.text: Net income was $1,066M on $1,935M of revenue — a 55% margin, helped by an income-tax bill of just $15M.

takeaways.title: Stock pay is the hidden cost
takeaways.text: Stock-based compensation was $265M — 14% of revenue. Excluding it and related payroll taxes, adjusted operating income was $1,194M vs $912M on the GAAP view.

oneTimers: Stock-based compensation of $265M sits inside cost of revenue and operating expenses; excluding it and $17M of related employer payroll taxes, adjusted operating income was $1,194M (a 62% margin) instead of $912M.
otherDetail: Interest income of $77M on Palantir's cash pile plus $92M of other income — $169M added below operating profit (rounded from the release's thousands).
follow100Note: The rows reconcile to $100 within a cent of rounding.
footerNote: Net income here is Palantir's total net income of $1,066M; $1,062M is attributable to common stockholders (the rest belongs to noncontrolling interests). Palantir reports in thousands — revenue was exactly $1,935.5M — so figures are rounded to whole $M and nudged by less than $1M per line so each step ties exactly. Segment split (Government/Commercial) is from the 10-Q; the release itself only breaks out U.S. figures.
